decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: How Much Are Mineral Rights Worth: Due Diligence Step By Step
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is da6167122063ceba8043b7ea9ad3e208ccb8b525788ca5395a6dfcca3c64f371; all 7 declared official sources passed live access review.

MRX methodology claims remain bounded to its current first-party page; Texas State Library claims remain bounded to county record location and availability; RRC claims remain bounded to query distinctions, record classes, reporting units, lag, and corrections; IRS claims remain bounded to the general purpose of basis and recordkeeping.

The article uses no fabricated owners, deeds, wells, permits, production, payments, prices, forecasts, acreage, ownership decimals, valuation ranges, testimonials, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, accounting, engineering, investment, reserve, or valuation conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology identifies production history, decline context, operator evidence, royalty terms, commodity assumptions, discount rate, title and acreage, and any offer terms as dated inputs to a directional range with assumptions stated.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology to order the evidence, assumption, scenario, sensitivity, exclusion, and handoff checks behind a directional range; it does not certify a value, prove title or reserves, guarantee an outcome, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Texas State Library, Land and Property History Research (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas State Library explains that real-property records including deeds, surveys, liens, and tax records are maintained by the county where the property is located and that online and older-record availability varies.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses that guidance to identify the county-record source class in the ownership-evidence step; it does not claim that one record or online search proves chain of title, reservations, legal effect, or owner-specific ownership.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Online Research Queries (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The RRC research-query directory provides official routes for production, drilling permits, completions, wellbores, and related oil-and-gas records and identifies update cadences for several systems.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the directory to identify record classes and workflow order; it does not claim that the presence of a query result proves an interest match, ownership, payment entitlement, reserves, future production, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, About Oil and Gas Data Queries (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The RRC data-query guide explains that each query is one slice of a larger system, a wellbore may contain one or more completions, and wellbore, completion, lease, permit, field, operator, and API identifiers support different searches.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those distinctions to build a match-key sheet and prevent unsupported joins; it does not infer an owner interest, tract match, payment, reserves, development outcome, or value from one identifier.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Well Records (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The RRC well-records guide describes records spanning drilling-permit applications, completion reports, plugging reports, plats, logs, and other documents and lists match fields used to request or search those records.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the guide to order development-evidence classification from application through later observed records; it does not equate a permit, completion filing, nearby record, or wellbore with production, economics, owner participation, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data Query System FAQs (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The RRC production FAQ states that Texas production is reported by lease, online information has a two-month lag, and operator reports can later be revised, corrected, or submitted delinquently.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses those statements to require reporting-unit, period, lag, correction, and interest-match checks before modeling; it does not infer individual-well allocation, title, payment entitlement, reserves, future production, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 551, Basis of Assets (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 551 describes basis as an amount used for tax computations including depreciation, depletion, and gain or loss and directs taxpayers to keep records of items affecting basis.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the publication only to separate basis records from a current directional value range and to require a qualified tax handoff; it does not calculate basis, gain, loss, depletion, tax liability, or an owner-specific tax result.
